simple.meaning: גֹּמֶד (gômed) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, a span.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גֹּמֶד (H1574) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גֹּמֶד (H1574) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גֹּמֶד (gômed) / H1574 is traced through Judges 3:16 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Ehud made himself a sword which had two edges, a cubit* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. in length; and he wore it under his clothing on his right thigh.
